target_customer: Commodity buyers, farmers and transporters in Ghana
problem: Buying and selling grain in Ghana was fragmented; the platform matched buyers' quantity, grade and price with sellers and handled weighing, grading and delivery.
business_model: Commodity trading marketplace with logistics margin

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace software was simple; the hard part was physical logistics and quality grading in Ghana.

defensibility.rationale: Matching buyers and sellers could build liquidity, but operations were manual and the team was three people.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; Ghana's formal commodity exchange only began full operation in late 2018 per IGC.

market_need_then: Ghana's maize trade was dominated by small private traders, mostly women, per policy papers, suggesting fragmentation and middleman margins.

branding.domain_note: Used tradeghana.co, a country suffixed domain, since the .com is generic

brand_strength.rationale: Very generic name and no press about the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Trade tried to build a commodity exchange for Ghana with a three person team. The YC directory marks it inactive, but no shutdown announcement, post mortem or dated funding history was found, so the cause of failure is not public and no failure factors are asserted.
notes: Cause of inactivity not public. Village.ai lists about $2.7M raised including Gates Foundation; single aggregator, unverified, not recorded as a round. Search for founder and funding found nothing. The YC page lists the location as Broken Arrow, OK. Website tradeghana.co not fetched. Exit type unknown because no source documents a shutdown beyond the YC status. Completeness pass: the 2.6M seed announced 2017-03-20 rests on a single database (Startup List Africa, which gives 2.7M over 3 rounds; lead investor undisclosed). It is matched to this company by name, Ghana commodity focus and YC W17 batch; the Gates Foundation mention in Village was not confirmed.
